[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-10.77): Good afternoon, Claire. Adrian Lim speaking. Thank you for calling. Are you somewhere comfortable to talk, or would you like a moment to settle down before we start?
[seg_0002] Client (11.16-19.00): Hello, Adrian. I'm at home, so it's quite quiet. I've brought my notebook over to the table. Just let me put my glasses on.
[seg_0003] Advisor (19.41-25.12): Of course, no hurry. May I have your identification details for our check, please?
[seg_0004] Client (25.52-32.58): My FIN is F seven nine nine seven nine one seven Y. My date of birth is 24 July 1962.
[seg_0005] Advisor (32.98-41.34): Thank you, Claire. We can take things at a comfortable pace today. I recommend buying Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund.
[seg_0006] Client (41.74-52.18): Okay, noted. These telephone appointments are convenient. I can keep my papers spread out instead of carrying everything into town. I've just come in from tending to my plants, actually.
[seg_0007] Advisor (52.58-59.92): That's a pleasant way to spend the afternoon. Have you been gardening for a while, or is it something you've started recently?
[seg_0008] Client (60.32-69.54): Quite recently, lah. Mostly herbs on the balcony, nothing too ambitious. My neighbour gave me some cuttings, and now I find myself checking on them every morning.
[seg_0009] Advisor (69.94-101.17): Nice to have a little routine like that. Let me turn to the items for today's discussion. So your objective remains long-term growth through a diversified investment, with a balance between growth potential and stability. For Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund, the equity holdings can pull the fund's value down when stock markets fall, while its fixed-income holdings can decline when interest rates rise. Do you understand how stock-market declines and rising interest rates can affect the fund's value?
[seg_0010] Client (101.58-109.11): Yes, I understand that falling stock markets can affect the equity holdings, and rising interest rates can reduce the value of the fixed-income holdings.
[seg_0011] Advisor (109.51-119.06): The transaction fee is 0.5% of the subscription amount. Can you confirm whether you are willing to accept investment losses within your planned allocation?
[seg_0012] Client (119.45-131.09): Yes, I am willing to accept investment losses and fluctuations, provided this stays within my planned allocation. I'll just turn to the relevant page in my notebook now. I put a tab in it, but it seems to have slipped.
[seg_0013] Advisor (131.49-136.29): Take your time. I'm here, and there's no need to rush through your papers.
[seg_0014] Client (136.69-148.31): Here we are. The fund I want to transact in is Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund. Please use euros as the transaction currency. Looking at my allocation notes, the amount I want to subscribe is 1,000,000.
[seg_0015] Advisor (148.71-153.47): I'll give you a moment with the page. Let me know when you're ready to continue.
[seg_0016] Client (153.87-163.45): Sorry, I read the overall budget rather than the subscription entry. Change the subscription amount to 75,000. My handwriting is rather cramped in this part of the notebook.
[seg_0017] Advisor (163.85-168.89): No problem, Claire. I'll stay on the line while you finish looking through it.
[seg_0018] Client (169.29-187.39): Actually, that entry was provisional; I've now found my completed allocation decision. The final subscription amount is 150,000, replacing what I just said. The quantity for this transaction is 2,000 units. I want to buy those units. Please place a limit order with a limit price of 75 euros per unit.
[seg_0019] Advisor (187.79-204.06): With your corrections applied, your final instruction is to buy 2,000 units of Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund for 150,000 euros, using a limit order at a limit price of 75 euros per unit. Do you confirm this instruction?
[seg_0020] Client (204.46-208.90): Yes, I confirm that final instruction with the corrected amount. Please proceed.
[seg_0021] Advisor (209.30-218.93): Thank you, Claire. That brings us to the end of today's call. I've also noted your preference for speaking by telephone when we arrange appointments.
[seg_0022] Client (219.33-225.34): Thanks, Adrian. That suits me much better. I'll put my notebook away now and get back to my afternoon.
[seg_0023] Advisor (225.74-229.78): You're welcome. Enjoy the rest of your day, and goodbye.

sub_criteria.note: The advisor explained specific concrete risks of the recommended fund, explaining how falling stock markets affect equity holdings and rising interest rates affect fixed-income holdings.

results.reasoning: The advisor clearly explained concrete risks associated with the recommended Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund, detailing the impact of stock market declines on equity holdings and interest rate rises on fixed-income holdings. sub_criteria.note: The advisor explicitly asked whether the client understood the key risks disclosed for the fund, and the client confirmed her understanding.

pricing disclosures 26 as part of their  order taking standards 27. This means  PBs should

disclosed to clients on a timely basis, with their agreement or “no objection”  properly 
documented. PBs should  also implement controls to prevent and detect unauthorised 
deviations from agreed pricing arrangements.

account opening or prior to the client’s first order taking. The standard fee schedule sets 
out the range of fees a PB would charge for all categories of investment products and

(a) to provide any information requested by the financial adviser in 
accordance with paragraph 11; or

the sales of riskier products to these clients. Instances were also noted where clients were

reflect RMs’ lack of risk consciousness and adopting a perfunctory approach towards the 
risk profiling exercise. MAS expects PBs to inculcate the right mindset and understanding

Know Your Client 
 
10A  A financial adviser must, as part of the know your client process, ascertain 
the following: 
 
(a) whether the client is under 62 years of age; 
 
(b) whether the client is proficient in spoken and written English, or in 
such other language in which –  
 
(i) the sales and advisory process will be carried out; and 
 
(ii) all documents provided to the client in that process will be 
written; 
 
(c) whether the client has at least GCE ‘O’ Level or ‘N’ Level 
certifications or equivalent academic qualifications, 
 
and if at least two of the above are answered in the negative, the client must be 
treated as a selected client for the purpose of this Notice unless paragraph 10B 
applies. 
[FAA-N16 (Amendment) 2025]

paragraph 10A as a selected client if  the financial adviser has reasons to 
conclude that the client possesses adequate knowledge and experience in any

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
